newsitem.title: USA: OPEC mulls raising crude target price - Lukman.
newsitem.headline: OPEC mulls raising crude target price - Lukman.

text.p: OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman said continued higher crude oil prices could prompt the cartel to raise its target price from the current $21 a barrel.
"If we have sustained higher prices, then we may have to look at that target price," Lukman said in a speech at Cambridge Energy Research Associates' energy forum in Houston.

The average price of the OPEC crude basket rose to $23.23 a barrel in January from $18.06 a barrel in January 1996, prompting Lukman to question whether the increase was temporary or marked a new "threshold" for oil prices.
OPEC's target price is used as a barometer by oil ministers of the producing countries to monitor the balance of global supply and demand.
"Price is like a thermometer. It tells us what is happening in the market," Lukman said.

Lukman told reporters OPEC has been approached by some producing countries in the former Soviet Union, Africa and Latin America about joining the cartel. "It would be premature for me to divulge the names," he said.
"We are hopeful that even if no other countries are added to OPEC, the level of cooperation between us and non-OPEC countries is increasing," Lukman said in a press conference after his speech.
OPEC also is seeking closer ties to consuming countries to assess oil demand and set production quotas.
"People are talking a more common language now and trying to iron out the rough spots of supply and demand," he said.
